questions.q: What changes when a COPY INTO load moves from a Snowflake worksheet to an Airflow task?
options: The SQL syntax of COPY INTO changes completely
COPY INTO can no longer load from a stage
Snowflake requires a different statement when Airflow is involved
Only what runs it — the statement itself is the same, now executed by a scheduled task instead of pasted in by hand
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: COPY INTO doesn't change — Airflow just becomes the thing that runs it, on a schedule.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which operator does Airflow's own current documentation recommend for running SQL against Snowflake?
options: BashOperator only
PythonOperator only
A dedicated SnowflakeOperator that is still the current standard
SQLExecuteQueryOperator, a general-purpose SQL operator pointed at a Snowflake conn_id
questions.explain: Airflow's Snowflake provider docs replaced the old SnowflakeOperator page with SQLExecuteQueryOperator — a tutorial still showing SnowflakeOperator is outdated.

questions.q: Per the lesson, when is Snowpipe the better fit compared to a scheduled Airflow COPY INTO load?
options: Snowpipe cannot load CSV files
Snowpipe is always strictly better in every situation
When files arrive unpredictably throughout the day and need to load within seconds to minutes, with no external scheduler
When the load must be one coordinated step inside a larger multi-task pipeline
questions.explain: Snowpipe is event-driven and near-instant with no scheduler; Airflow is preferred when the load needs coordination with other pipeline steps.

questions.q: In the SQLExecuteQueryOperator example, what does `conn_id="snowflake_default"` provide?
options: The name of the DAG
The file format for the COPY INTO statement
The Connection Airflow uses to reach the correct Snowflake account/credentials
The retry count for the task
questions.explain: conn_id references a stored Connection (Chapter 3) — it's how the task knows where and how to connect to Snowflake.

questions.q: What does the lesson say actually appears in the Airflow task log when copy_into_orders runs?
options: Only a generic 'task succeeded' message with no detail
The dbt build output
The real COPY INTO result Snowflake returns — file name, rows parsed, rows loaded, and any errors
Nothing; Airflow suppresses all SQL output
questions.explain: The task log shows Snowflake's actual COPY INTO result, the same output you'd see running it in a worksheet.
